column1: # guarded-commands.tsv — the tracked catalogue of destructive commands the `guard-gaps` sweep class probes
# against the wired PreToolUse guard (feature 010, FR-021). DANGER-OK: every `command` cell below is probe
# DATA; the class pipes it to the guard's stdin as a synthetic tool call and reads the guard's refusal. No row
# is ever executed. `expected` is what this repository's governance requires of the guard (refused); the class
# records what the guard actually did, and a destructive command it lets through is a finding classified
# third-party (the guard is upstream code in submodules/constitution; reporting route: upstream issue).
# Adding a command is a data change here plus the class's corpus. `source` names where the command class is
# stated in a tracked document. `candidate` is the extended regex naming the dangerous command CLASS the row
# stands for (`-` when the row names none): the class requires at least one `refused` row whose command
# matches it, so a row softened below its class or a class flipped to `allowed` is a drift finding. This
# column replaces the hand CANDIDATES list the class used to carry (class review rev-safety ruling).
